subject: Parlane edge adapter warmup plan + cutover failover checklist
messages:
From: Raf Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Cleo Harris <cleo@parklane.co>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: [Action] Edge adapter warmup & cutover window proposal

Hi Cleo —

Great talking yesterday. Per our call, attached is a concise plan for the Parklane edge-adapter cutover and warmup so we hit latency SLOs on day-one without surprising token costs. High level asks from Parklane: low-latency for search/autocomplete and stable 99th pct for 2s budget on small queries.

Quick summary of the plan inside:
- Pre-warm strategy: synthetic prefix requests to populate KV cache and JIT paths for common models.
- Traffic shaping: gradual 10%, 30%, 60%, 100% shift over a 6-hour window with active health checks.
- Rate-fence: 2-tier throttles (dev vs prod) and transparent 429 semantics.
- Rollback policy: instant traffic revert to previous gateway with automatic fallback to quantized variant.

Please confirm the 6-hour maintenance window on Aug 14 00:00–06:00 UTC or propose an alternate. I attached a short checklist and sample adapter code — the sample contains warmup curl loops and a Node snippet for prefetching prompts.

Attachments: parklane-edge-warmup-checklist.pdf (short checklist), sdk-adapter-samples.tar.gz (code), mvp-mutual-action-plan.xlsx

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm the window and list of model endpoints to prewarm (model ids or paths).
2) We run a dry-run in staging with the warmup script and share telemetry (p90/p99 latency, KV hit rate).
3) Day-of: Redwood on-call + Parklane infra lead on call; we execute the staged traffic shift.

Thanks — Raf
Raf Mendes
Customer Success – Redwood Inference

From: Cleo Harris <cleo@parklane.co>
To: Raf Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Platform Team <platform@parklane.co>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 10:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [Action] Edge adapter warmup & cutover window proposal

Raf — thanks, this looks sensible.

Aug 14 00:00–06:00 UTC works for us. We'll target these model endpoints for pre-warm (internal names):
- search-v2 (short queries)
- suggest-autocomplete (prefix heavy)
- rerank-mini (3-5 candidates)

Couple of asks:
- Can the warmup script stop/exit if it sees sustained 5xx? We need fail-fast behaviour so we don't mask infra issues.
- For rate-fence, we want a soft-429 at 80% of configured capacity so our platform can start backpressure earlier; is that configurable?

I'll loop Jermaine (infra lead) if we need infra-level routing changes. He prefers Slack but I'll also send a calendar invite.

Cleo
Cleo Harris
Head of Platform — Parklane

From: Raf Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 11:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Parklane warmup pattern + config notes (for implementation)

Team — copying the plan I sent Parklane. Key implementation points for the engineering handoff:

1) Warmup semantics (how the script behaves)
- Exponential ramp of synthetic requests with model-seen prefixes. Each request attaches headers: X-Redwood-Warmup: 1 and X-Trace-Id.
- Stop condition: if >5% of requests return 5xx in a 2-minute sliding window, script exits and notifies via PagerDuty. (Cleo requested fail-fast.)

2) Pre-warm payloads (attached samples in sdk-adapter-samples.tar.gz)
- Use short prefixed prompts (<=32 tokens) to load KV cache and compile hot paths. Example Node snippet included.

3) Retries/timeouts & backoff
- Client-side: 3 retry attempts with full jitter backoff (initial 250ms). For idempotent pre-warm calls we can be more aggressive.
- Server-side: observe 429 headers (X-Rate-Fence: level, X-Quota-Remaining) and return structured info in JSON so Parklane can surface graceful degradation.

4) Rate-fencing behaviour
- Add a soft-429 threshold at 80% of operational capacity (configurable on a per-route basis).
- 429 responses include Retry-After (seconds) and a short diagnostic token for Redwood to trace the cause.

5) Cutover window steps (day-of runbook)
- 00:00 UTC: Toggle canary to 10% traffic, run 15m smoke tests.
- 00:45 UTC: Increase to 30%, validate p99 and error budgets.
- 02:00 UTC: 60% traffic if metrics stable.
- 04:00 UTC: 100% traffic and keep 2-hour watch.
- Any p99 spike >1.5x baseline or >3% error rate -> immediate revert to previous gateway.

6) Observability hooks
- Add per-route tracing header: X-Redwood-Trace and include sample dashboards in the drive folder.

I attached a concise checklist (parklane-edge-warmup-checklist.pdf) and a tarball with sample code. Monica, can you author the final runbook with commands and timing? Vivek, please confirm fallback variant availability (quantized/cheaper model) in the target pool.

Thanks — Raf

From: Cleo Harris <cleo@parklane.co>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Raf Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jermaine Lo <jermaine.lo@parklane.co>, Platform Team <platform@parklane.co>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [Action] Edge adapter warmup & cutover window proposal

Thanks everyone — Jermaine confirmed the window and routed the DNS failover to our previous gateway for immediate revert. We have two follow-ups before the dry-run on Aug 10:

1) Please include a script flag --max-errors=N for warmup so we can set N=10 on staging and N=25 in prod.
2) Can Redwood include the soft-429 behavior in response body with a short code we can check programmatically (example: {"code": "RATE_FENCE_SOFT", "capacity_pct": 82})?

If you can update the checklist with those two items I'll mark the plan green. Calendar invite coming.

Cleo
Head of Platform — Parklane
